flow_ref: User story (not in any OCMS flow deck)
code_summary: thirdpartyapi workflows/cesTpApiARelay (CesCreateNoticeController /v1/cesWebhook-create-notice, service/CesNopoServiceImpl: validation, subscription key check, forward through APIM, audit). ocmsadminapi workflows/notice_creation/core (CreateNoticeController /cesWebhook-create-notice, CreateNoticeServiceImpl.processEHTWebhook, helpers/ValidationServices, NoticeProcessingHelper, NoticeRecordHelper), auth/filter/JwtFilter. ocmsadminprivateapi, ocmsadminui, ocmseserviceapi, ocmseserviceui: not relevant to this story
note: Status in the sheet: 'Fully paid'. There is no OCMS flow deck, so 'Sesuai' means the code does what the story text says. Story remark: ready when EHT provides the API doc, same spec as the Certis document. The code that exists is the Certis/CES webhook (labels 030-999): real-time receipt, validation, VON/OND/eVON/eOND saved, AN with PS-ANS, UPL, starting stage, audit and reply. All of that behaviour is Sesuai for the CES path, but the first step is Sebagian because nothing in the repo proves that 'EHT' in the story is Certis; other EHT-named paths exist too (label 023 REPCCS_EHT on the REPCCS webhook, the ehtsftp-create-notice endpoint) and the 'EHT webhook' path itself only accepts owner CES (CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:349). If URA confirms EHT = Certis, that step moves to Sesuai. Maintenance tickets (all Closed/Prod deployed, not lowering any fit): OCMS-DF-2026-100, OCMS-DF-2026-154, OCMS-DF-2026-115. Not provable from the repo: APIM/WAF configuration, the subscription key value, subsystem label and offence rule code table content per environment, and the EHT API specification. ocmsadminapi /v1/cesWebhook-create-notice is open without JWT and without a key (only the relay checks the key).
recommendation: Can be claimed for notice receipt on the Certis/CES path. Confirm with URA whether EHT uses the same CES path; if yes, the first step becomes Sesuai. Block direct external access to ocmsadminapi /v1/cesWebhook-create-notice if possible.

steps.step: The EHT system sends each parking offence notice to OCMS in real time through one webhook call and OCMS accepts it immediately
steps.detail: The code only has a Certis/CES path, not a path named EHT: Certis calls thirdpartyapi POST /v1/cesWebhook-create-notice (CesCreateNoticeController.java:22-25); the relay compares Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key with Key Vault (CesNopoServiceImpl.java:165-178), forwards it synchronously through APIM (:182) to ocmsadminapi /v1/cesWebhook-create-notice (path in application-prod.properties:22, CreateNoticeController.java:103-109, processEHTWebhook in CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:284), and the notice is created in the same request. The real-time behaviour is proven. What is not proven: that the 'EHT' sender in the story is this Certis system. Ticket OCMS-DF-2026-100 calls the sender 'CES/EHT' and the report UI uses the 'EHT' layout for the CES source (ReportListNoticeFE.tsx:81-83), but other EHT-named paths exist too: label 023 REPCCS_EHT is accepted on the REPCCS webhook (RepWebHookPayloadValidator.java:204-211) and ehtsftp-create-notice (CreateNoticeController.java:97-101). The story remark says the EHT spec equals the Certis document and the EHT API doc is not yet given: cannot verify from repo. ocmsadminapi /v1/cesWebhook-create-notice is open without JWT (JwtFilter.java:180) and without a key check; the key is only checked in the thirdpartyapi relay.

steps.step: Notice data is checked before it is accepted (subsystem label 030-999 owned by CES, mandatory fields, field lengths, offence rule code)
steps.detail: The thirdpartyapi relay checks field lengths (PayloadLengthValidator, CesNopoServiceImpl.java:80), the first 3 digits of the subsystem label 030-999 (:96-108) and notice no positions 2-4 also 030-999, then mandatory fields (:110-155). ocmsadminapi checks the label exists in the database and its owner is CES (CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:340-355) and that the offence rule code exists in the table for that vehicle category (ValidationServices.java:165-188, called at :375-378). All failures are answered to Certis as a failure appCode (CesNopoServiceImpl.java:206-256). Subsystem label and rule code data in the database: cannot verify from repo.

steps.step: A received Notice of Parking Offence (NOPO) is saved as a new notice in the intranet (VON, OND) and internet (eVON, eOND) records
steps.detail: After validation and the duplicate check (CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:359-364), createNoticeRecord (:1195) prepares the entities and batchSaveNoticeRecords (:811-812, CreateNoticeHelper.java:251) saves VON/OND in the intranet and then eVON/eOND in the internet (payment.sync.enabled=true in application-prod.properties:4). The relay only answers OCMS-2000 to Certis when ocmsadminapi answers OK; any other appCode, including unknown ones, is answered as a failure (CesNopoServiceImpl.java:206-256, last branch :251-256). Related tickets, all Closed/Prod deployed and not lowering any fit: OCMS-DF-2026-100 (notice 618800040C existed in the internet without an intranet VON; saves separated and is_sync), OCMS-DF-2026-154 (backend failures reported as success to Certis; the code on main now answers failure for an unknown appCode), OCMS-DF-2026-115 (403 from the Azure WAF before reaching the application: infrastructure, cannot verify from repo).

steps.step: A received Advisory Notice (AN, an_flag Y from the sender) is recognised and saved as an AN with PS-ANS
steps.detail: The an_flag from Certis is passed on by the relay (CesNopoServiceImpl.java:370). For labels 030-999, checkANSForEHT passes the notice when an_flag is Y, a vehicle number exists and the offence type is not empty or 0 (NoticeProcessingHelper.java:154-187). The notice is then created with permanent suspension PS-ANS, payment not allowed and ANS eservice message (CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:1056-1096), and the PS-ANS suspended_notice row is saved together with the VON (NoticeRecordHelper.java:324-330, 496-512). The earlier 2-year offence check is deliberately commented out as 'for next epic' (NoticeProcessingHelper.java:181-186): the AN decision rests entirely on the sender flag. This differs from the REPCCS path in OCMS3.1, which does not create PS-ANS; the difference is real in the code (CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:764 in ocmsadminprivateapi exists only in the CES branch).

steps.step: An unauthorised use of parking lots (UPL) notice with no vehicle number is recognised and saved
steps.detail: The relay recognises VehicleCategory 0, VehicleRegistration X and LicencePlate N.A as UPL and gives offence type U (CesNopoServiceImpl.java:383-388). ocmsadminapi overwrites that offence type with the rule code table lookup (ValidationServices.java:188), maps vehicle number N.A to vehicle registration type X (CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:1018) and runs setProcessingStagesForX (:1147): payment N, composition_amount 0, next stage DN1 (NoticeProcessingHelper.java:390-409). Same as the REPCCS path in OCMS3.1. Whether the rule code row for category 0 exists in the database: cannot verify from repo.

steps.step: A saved notice gets its starting processing stage so OCMS can start processing it
steps.detail: V/S/D vehicles get last stage NPA, next stage ROV, payment allowed (NoticeProcessingHelper.java:422-440). Type X gets next stage DN1 with payment blocked (:390-409). An AN notice gets NPA/ROV plus the PS-ANS suspension (CreateNoticeServiceImpl.java:1069-1085). All are filled before the VON is saved (:1147-1150). The downstream crons that pick up ROV/DN1 belong to other stories and were not traced.

steps.step: Every receipt is recorded in the audit transaction table and the sender gets the result at once (OK or rejected); failures can be traced
steps.detail: Every exit of the relay saves an audit row through saveAuditOnce with statusNum 0 for success and 1 for failure (CesNopoServiceImpl.java:259, 453-490), including validation failures, a wrong key and a failure appCode from ocmsadminapi (:206-256). An unexpected exception in the controller is saved through saveAuditForError (CesCreateNoticeController.java:58-65). The sender gets a JSON appCode and message in the same request. The 'Notices Created by Enforcement Systems' report reads these status 1 audit rows for the CES source (EnforcementServiceImpl.java:346-376). Unlike REPCCS in OCMS3.1, where failures inside createNotice are not marked in the audit.
